summary: Cypress packs nearly 50,000 people into just 6.6 square miles — a density north of 7,500 per square mile — yet the landscape reads as almost entirely single-family residential, pancake-flat, and startlingly quiet for something wedged between Buena Park, Stanton, and Los Alamitos in the heart of northwest Orange County. That flatness is the defining geographic fact: no hills, no vistas, no dramatic terrain, just a compact grid of mid-century and newer homes stretching in every direction, bisected by Lincoln Avenue and Katella Avenue's commercial strips. The median household income of $124,167 against an $870,100 median home price yields a price-to-income ratio just above 7:1 — tight but not as punishing as coastal OC, and rents around $2,454 keep the squeeze noticeable for anyone not already holding equity. Employment leans heavily on the surrounding corridor — Cypress sits minutes from major medical centers, logistics hubs near the 605 and 405 freeways, and retail anchors like Los Cerritos Center just across the county line — making it functionally a bedroom community where most residents commute outward. The climate is genuinely mild, averaging 75°F daytime highs and 56°F lows with 9.4 hours of daily sunshine, which makes the city's scattered parks and the paved paths along flood-control channels usable year-round. Schools post strong numbers: an average ELA score 51.9 points above standard and a 96.9% graduation rate across 11 campuses. Cypress is the kind of place whose greatest asset — affordable-for-OC stability in a mild climate — is also its limitation: very little changes here, by design.
